documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Technology Usage Guidelines
documents.summary: An IT-office guideline for all students, employees and third parties using AI on university resources. It welcomes responsible use, recommends Copilot, and spends most of its text on data protection, verification of output, vendor risk review, security and monitoring. A single paragraph on academic integrity points to UAM 6,502 and says AI use should be disclosed as appropriate.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines "advocate for fostering curiosity and responsible usage of AI tools" and recommend Microsoft Copilot, so AI use is welcomed with conditions on data protection, verification and risk review. They defer to UAM 6,502 for academic integrity and say users should "disclose the use of AI in academic settings as appropriate" but set no course-level rule, so permit with conditions rather than delegates.

documents.summary: Official UNR AI-site guidance for instructors on writing a syllabus statement. It recommends including a statement and discussing it on day one, then gives sample language for permitted, partly allowed and banned courses, tied to the academic integrity policy UAM 6,502. The banned sample lists four prohibited actions.
documents.stance_why: The page tells instructors to write their own AI statement and offers three sample statements ("AI use allowed", "AI use partially allowed", "AI use not permitted") because views "fall loosely into 3 categories".
